source_record: Live DB: Ezekiel 27:32 word_id 238432, pointed בְּנִיהֶם֙, Strong's H5204, morphology HR/Ncmsc/Sp3mp. No local textual qere row is attached to this word. Isolated shadow candidate group 504, signature בּניהם֙: sons member root_id 6627/root בני, בְּנֵיהֶם֙, H1121, HNcmpc/Sp3mp, occurrences Jer 11:22 word_id 213637 and Jer 17:2 word_id 215100; wailing member root_id 21384/root ני, בְּנִיהֶם֙, H5204, HR/Ncmsc/Sp3mp, occurrence Ezek 27:32 word_id 238432.
independent_evidence: BDB H5204 marks the MT lexical reading as doubtful and reports בְּנֵיהֶם ('their sons') in 11 MSS, early editions, LXX, Arabic, Theodotion, and Syriac. The Greek LXX text displayed for Ezekiel 27:32 reads καὶ λήμψονται οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ σὲ θρῆνον ('and their sons will take up a lament for you'), aligning with 'their sons'. Local word_variants for word_id 238432 has no qere row. YLT DB check: verse has 30 whitespace tokens but only 14 aligned positions; word_id 238432 is bridged to YLT positions 1 'And' and 2 'lifted', while word_id 238430 (וְנָשְׂאוּ, H5375) has no mapping and positions 7 'their' / 8 'sons' are unaligned. Translation comparison: YLT renders 'their sons'; KJV/JPS 1917 render 'in their wailing'; NET renders 'as they wail'. NET's Dahood note concerns the later כְּדֻמָה, not בְּנִיהֶם. The translation divergence does not establish the original Hebrew reading.
assessment: A genuine textual/lexical ambiguity under the same consonantal spelling: MT בְּנִיהֶם is parsed as 'in their wailing'; multiple witnesses and LXX support בְּנֵיהֶם ('their sons'). Keep the MT token and external-witness reading separate. This is not a Masoretic qere unless the source apparatus explicitly says so. The existing YLT alignment is also a strong U-1 anomaly: it appears to map the MT H5204 word to 'And/lifted' while leaving the YLT 'their sons' phrase unaligned. This does not authorize changes to the translation or alignment. The LXX 'their sons' corresponds to the existing sons member of group 504; MT Ezekiel remains the separate wailing member. The cross-root orthographic link is verified, but textual priority remains open. The LXX and the reported Hebrew/version witnesses support the sons reading, while several translations retain the MT wailing reading. Textual priority remains unresolved; do not let the YLT rendering itself determine the Hebrew witness.
next_action: Preserve MT and LXX readings separately. If YLT alignment work resumes, review the 14/30 mapped positions in this verse as a separate U-1 task; do not recompute or rewrite alignments during this Hebrew variant review.

source_record: Live DB: Numbers 13:21 word_id 47351, pointed לְבֹ֥א, H935, morphology HNp; Numbers 34:8 word_id 55394, pointed לְבֹ֣א, H935, morphology HNp. The project's pinned OSHB source commit is 3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f.
independent_evidence: WLC analyses for Numbers 13:21 and 34:8 parse לְבֹא with H935 verbally. UBS Handbook recommends 'Lebo-hamath' in Num 13:21, noting the name in 1 Kgs 8:65, while also preserving the entrance/pass interpretation. Live DB occurrence audit: Num 13:21 word_id 47351 and Num 34:8 word_id 55394 are both HNp/root לבא; Josh 13:5 (72946), Judg 3:3 (77824), Ezek 47:15 (245631) are HNp/root לבוא; 1 Kgs 8:65 (111942) is HR/Np; 2 Kgs 14:25 (124316) is HR/Ncmsc. The source uses both toponymic and common-noun analyses by context.
assessment: The HNp source annotation for the two Numbers tokens is defensible and consistent with other boundary-place occurrences. H935 is compatible with the name's etymological relationship to בוא ('come/enter'). The literal 'entrance of Hamath' / 'Hamath Pass' interpretation remains a valid translation alternative; this is not a confirmed source-data defect.
next_action: No source correction. Preserve HNp, H935, root לבא, and pointed forms. Document the toponymic reading and literal entrance/pass alternative. Do not merge the plene לבוא forms because matres are retained by the strict rule.

source_record: Live DB: 2 Kings 19:13 word_id 126492 and Isaiah 37:13 word_id 202764; both pointed לָעִ֣יר, Strong's H5892, morphology HNp. Project source mapping is pinned to OSHB commit 3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f.
independent_evidence: WLC analyses for 2 Kings 19:13 and Isaiah 37:13 assign H5892 and parse לָעִיר as common noun 'city'. UBS Handbook on 2 Kings 19:13 reports that some interpreters take laʿir as a separate place-name Lahir/Lair, and judges this the most likely reading in 2 Kings 19:13. The parallel Isaiah verse preserves the same ambiguity. Project parser passes OSHB @morph verbatim; HNp is likely an upstream annotation.
assessment: The Lair proper-name reading has substantial historical-geographical support. Zadok (1976) identifies Lair with L'r in Aršam's letters and Lahiru in northeastern Babylonia, and notes Lahiru became an Assyrian province. The UBS Handbook and NET notes likewise favor Lair. The project's HNp morphology is therefore a defensible intentional annotation, not a likely parser error. The common-noun reading 'the city of Sepharvaim' remains a genuine translation alternative; preserve both in notes and do not alter stored Strong's or morphology.
next_action: No source correction. Retain HNp and H5892. Add the Lair toponym identification and common-noun alternative to the study guide, citing Zadok (1976), UBS Handbook, and NET notes.
